config.title: Build webhook receiver with signature verification

intro.title: Build webhook receiver with signature verification
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a secure webhook receiver in Node.js that validates incoming requests using signature verification. You will learn how to handle HTTP POST requests, parse JSON payloads, and compute HMAC signatures to ensure data integrity and authenticity. The core programming concepts involve using the built-in crypto module for hashing and comparing signatures, and the Express.js framework for setting up a web server. By the end, you will have a functional endpoint that can safely process webhook events from external services.
intro.usecase: Webhook receivers with signature verification are essential for secure integrations in real-world applications like payment gateways (e.g., Stripe), notification services (e.g., Slack or GitHub), and e-commerce platforms (e.g., Shopify). Developers implement this pattern to ensure data integrity and authenticity when external services send automated updates to dashboards, order management systems, or user activity logs. For instance, a payment confirmation webhook updates a merchant's admin panel only after verifying the signature, preventing fraudulent transactions. This security measure is critical in production environments where handling sensitive data via HTTP callbacks is common.

objectives: Construct a Node.js Express server to receive webhook payloads
Configure environment variables to store webhook secrets securely
Implement signature verification logic using HMAC cryptography
Initialize middleware to parse incoming webhook request bodies
Apply validation checks to ensure webhook authenticity
Manipulate request headers to extract signature information
Integrate error handling for failed signature verification
